captions.instagram:
How do AI video models work?

Every AI video starts as pure static. Watch a real diffusion model pull a picture out of noise in your browser, steer it with a prompt, see why frames flicker when they are made one at a time, and test whether a hidden watermark survives an edit.

→ A video is a stack of still pictures: 24 of them every second in cinema.
→ One second of Full HD is about 149 million numbers. Text is a few words.
→ Diffusion starts from pure static, guesses the picture, removes a little noise, and repeats.
→ Models first squeeze video into a small latent cube, then cut it into space-time patches.
→ A prompt steers every denoising step. Here: "a blue square".

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/videomodelclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How do AI video models work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Every AI video starts as pure static. Watch a real diffusion model pull a picture out of noise in your browser, steer it with a prompt, see why frames flicker when they are made one at a time, and test whether a hidden watermark survives an edit.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/videomodelclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/videomodelclear

In this video:
• A video is a huge stack of numbers. Frames stacked over time make a space-time cube.
• Diffusion: noise in, picture out. Models learn to guess the clean picture hidden under noise.
• Squeeze, then cut into patches. An autoencoder squeezes video into a small latent cube, about 48 times smaller in open models.
• Words steer every step. A text encoder turns the prompt into numbers the denoiser reads.
• Consistency is the hard part. Make each frame alone and the object teleports and changes colour.
• Costly, and easy to mistake for real. A 5-second clip took about 3.4 million joules in 2025 tests of open models, far more than a picture or a text reply.
